name: Schlaiten
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful mountain village in the Iseltal valley, with authentic charm and panoramic views of the Schobergruppe.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Schlaiten is situated in East Tyrol within the Lienz district on a sun-drenched terrace 150 metres above the Isel Valley at an elevation of 876 metres, home to around 450 residents. This serene mountain village nestles against the slopes of the Rotenstein (2,805 m) in the Villgraten Mountains, directly facing the imposing Schober Group. Schlaiten is distinguished by total tranquility, pristine alpine pastures, and an absence of transit traffic. The traditional hamlets of Mesnerdorf, Plon, and Gonzach provide sweeping panoramic views across the valley floor to the jagged limestone crags of the Lienz Dolomites, offering an idyllic retreat for walkers.

Geschichte

The name Schlaiten originates from a Slavic term meaning marshy meadow, denoting ancient wetland terraces. The community was first recorded in 1299 in the Gorizian land registry as vf dem Slaetten. Between the 13th and 15th centuries, Schlaiten experienced mining activity extracting silver, lead, and zinc along the Göriach stream, leaving historical mine adits intact today. The Late Gothic parish church of Saint Paul was first documented in 1458 and retains its 15th-century spire. During the 17th and 18th centuries, it gained widespread renown as a pilgrimage shrine dedicated to the Fourteen Holy Helpers. Schlaiten regained full municipal independence in 1949.

Anreise

Schlaiten is conveniently reached through the Isel Valley. Motorists arriving from the north take the Felbertauernstraße B108 highway past Mittersill and Matrei in Osttirol, turning off at St. Johann im Walde onto the panoramic L289 mountain road ascending directly to the plateau. From the south, access leads via the town of Lienz, situated roughly 15 kilometres away. Train passengers arrive at Lienz railway station along the Drau Valley railway. From Lienz, VVT regional bus lines 951 and 952 operate through the valley with local connections, free of charge for holders of the East Tyrol guest card.

Tipps

A memorable highlight is the panoramic vantage point from Schlaiten's mountain farmsteads, revealing the jagged peaks of the Lienz Dolomites and the glaciated summits of the Schober Group, including the Hochschober (3,242 m). Down on the valley floor, the 29-kilometre Iseltal cycle trail follows the last free-flowing glacial river of the Alps, offering wonderful cycling combinable with plateau hikes. Trekkers can ascend from Schlaiten across traditional pastures to the summit of the Rotenstein (2,805 m) or explore the nearby Hochschoberhütte alpine hut in Hohe Tauern National Park. History lovers can visit the medieval mining shafts in Göriachgraben.
